claims.claim: The composite model's timbre is 11 harmonics with amplitude 1/h (incon default), and the scoring timbre must equal the synthesis timbre.
Roughness is Hutchinson & Knopoff with the Mashinter 2006 parametrisation, cut off at y > 1.2 critical bandwidths and normalised by sum(A^2).

Harmonicity is Milne (2013) / Harrison & Pearce (2018) pitch-class harmonicity: Gaussian-smoothed circular spectrum (sigma 6.83 cents, rho 0.75) on a 1200-bin grid, cosine-similarity template sweep, KL from uniform in bits.

sources.title: incon R/model-har18.R and hrep R/milne-pc-spectrum.R port

claims.claim: Familiarity is defined only for chords whose intervals are within 20.0 cents of 12-TET; the test is strictly greater-than, so exactly 20.0 cents is inside. Otherwise the model drops to the count-weighted neutral log-probability -2.34127473752867.
claims.verified_by: tests/fixtures/familiarity.json; boundary probed at 19 and 21 cents

claims.claim: Composite score = 0.628434666589357 - 1.62001025973261*roughness + 1.77992362857478*harmonicity + 0.0892234643584134*logP, with the chord-size term disabled (weight 0).

sources.title: Simultaneous consonance in music perception and composition

claims.claim: On a 1-cent grid with 1200 bins, every candidate's pitch-class spectrum is an exact circular rotation of one precomputed single-note spectrum, so harmonicity over a candidate set can be computed by index shift rather than by rebuilding each spectrum.
claims.verified_by: max abs diff 1.665e-15 over 2401 candidates; 6.8x speedup in numpy alone

claims.claim: Candidate sets are built as: standard, step 1200/edo; free, uniform step resolution_cents; or free with snap_to, the given intervals repeated every octave and clipped to range. Endpoints use ceil((low-offset)/step) and floor((high-offset)/step), inclusive.
numpy's default_rng is PCG64 (XSL-RR 128/64); Generator.random() converts a raw uint64 to a double as (raw >> 11) * 2**-53.

sources.title: recorded raw uint64 and doubles for 7 seeds

claims.note: Corroborated rather than verified: the C++ implementation does not yet exist, so the conversion rule is asserted against recorded outputs but not yet reproduced. T-010 promotes it to verified.

claims.claim: generate_stream is deterministic given seed, configuration and candidate set: one RNG draw per note, drawn after the weight vector is built; any additional draw desynchronises every subsequent note.
claims.verified_by: streams regenerated and reproduced exactly; tests/fixtures/streams.json

claims.claim: Ableton Live supports MPE from version 11 onward; as of Live 12 all bundled Live instruments are MPE-capable, and MPE data can be drawn without an MPE controller.

sources.title: MPE in Live 11 and later FAQ

claims.claim: A 14-bit pitch bend over a +/-2 semitone range resolves 4 semitones / 16384 steps = 0.0244 cents per step; over +/-48 semitones it resolves 0.586 cents. Only the former meets the 0.05-cent budget in T-012.
claims.verified_by: arithmetic, and max_error_cents 0.05 recorded across 10 fixture pitches

claims.claim: Per-note generation in the Python reference costs about 12 ms in standard mode (25 candidates), 133 ms in free 5-cent mode (481 candidates) and 612 ms in free 1-cent mode (2401 candidates); harmonicity is roughly 91% of that cost.
claims.note: Measured on the planning sandbox, not on the target machine. The absolute numbers will differ; the ordering and the conclusion that generation cannot run on the audio thread will not. See R-002.

claims.claim: JUCE 8.0.15 is the highest tag on the 8.x line; the 9.x line has reached 9.0.2 (2026-09-07).
claims.verified_by: direct query of the official repository's tag list

claims.claim: JUCE 9.0.0 introduces 35+ breaking changes, including moving functions and types out of VST3ClientExtensions into a new VST3Interface struct behind a JUCE_VST3_COMPATIBLE_CLASSES define.
Ableton Live honours an MPE zone configuration (RPN 6) and member pitch-bend-range (RPN 0,0) emitted from a plugin's MIDI output and routed to another track.

sources.title: MPE in Live 11 and later FAQ

claims.note: The FAQ documents MPE input from controllers and MPE editing in clips. It does not state that a plugin's MIDI *output* can configure an MPE zone on a downstream track. This could not be verified in the planning sandbox because it requires a running Live installation. Carried into Phase 4 as R-006 (Medium) with a mitigation in S-012.
